Define a Gaussian random-intercept scenario

Source: R/groundtruth.R
gt_ri_scenario.Rd

Define a Gaussian random-intercept scenario

Usage

gt_ri_scenario(
  id,
  n_groups = 20L,
  group_sizes = 6L,
  alpha = 1,
  beta = 0.7,
  sigma = 1,
  tau = 0.5,
  x_level = "observation"
)

Arguments

id

A non-empty scalar character identifier.

n_groups

Number of groups, at least two.

group_sizes

A positive integer scalar repeated across groups, or one positive integer size for each group. At least one group must be replicated.

alpha

Population intercept.

beta

Population slope for x.

sigma

Positive residual standard deviation.

tau

Non-negative random-intercept standard deviation.

x_level

Either "observation" (one independent standard-normal predictor per observation; the default) or "group" (one independent standard-normal predictor per group, expanded to that group's observations in canonical group order).

Value

A gt_scenario for the Gaussian random-intercept model.

Details

Predictor draws are independent of random intercepts and residual errors. The conditional residual ICC given x is tau^2 / (tau^2 + sigma^2). A shared group-level predictor also contributes to unconditional same-group response correlation. The scenario records x_level and uses generator revision random-intercept-v2.

Examples

gt_ri_scenario("clusters", n_groups = 5L, group_sizes = 4L)
#> $id
#> [1] "clusters"
#> 
#> $n
#> [1] 20
#> 
#> $n_groups
#> [1] 5
#> 
#> $group_sizes
#> [1] 4 4 4 4 4
#> 
#> $alpha
#> [1] 1
#> 
#> $beta
#> [1] 0.7
#> 
#> $sigma
#> [1] 1
#> 
#> $tau
#> [1] 0.5
#> 
#> $x_level
#> [1] "observation"
#> 
#> $family
#> [1] "random_intercept"
#> 
#> attr(,"class")
#> [1] "gt_scenario"
